newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Gas pipeline explodes at Seoul construction site.
newsitem.headline: Gas pipeline explodes at Seoul construction site.

text.p: An underground gas pipeline exploded at a subway construction site in central Seoul on Thursday, but there were no casualties, police said.
Witnesses said a flame from the explosion reached up to 50 metres (160 feet) before it was brought under control after about 30 minutes by firemen.
A police officer said an excavator at the subway construction site hit the gas pipe before the blast at one of Seoul's busiest intersections. Traffic snarled for hours.
"We are investigating the exact cause of the explosion. No one was killed and the situation ended within half an hour," he said.
The blast took place near the site of another gas pipeline explosion in December 1994, which ripped through a nearby district destroying dozens of homes and shops and killed 12 people.

In April 1995, a gas blast at a subway construction site in the southwestern city of Taegu killed 100 people, most of them teenagers on their way to school. That explosion was caused by a welding torch, according to police.
